transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been having these thoughts that maybe it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone.
How long have you been having these thoughts about not wanting to wake up?

It’s been going on for a little while now. I keep finding myself thinking that maybe it would be easier if I just didn’t wake up. I haven’t made any plan to hurt myself, but the thought keeps coming back.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?
Yeah… after that burst of energy wore off, I’ve been feeling pretty down. It’s like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’ll just sit at the table staring at my coffee, feeling empty and kind of ashamed.
Have you lost interest in activities that you used to enjoy?

Yeah, I have. The stuff that usually helps me unwind—fishing, looking through old vinyl records, tailgating, even checking on my home-brew—it all just feels like work now. I kind of quit caring about it.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?
I don’t know… I haven’t really noticed feeling anxious exactly. Mostly I just feel worn down. Maybe a little tense sometimes, but I’m not sure I’d call it on edge.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight lately?
Yeah, a bit. I haven’t really been hungry most days—I kind of have to remind myself to eat. Supper just looks like too much trouble, and my jeans are fitting looser than they were.
Have you been feeling like you're moving slower than usual or having trouble getting things done?

Yeah… things have been taking me a lot longer. I’ve fallen behind on bills, missed callbacks and appointments, stuff like that. I needed to be looking for work, but I couldn’t keep at it steady. Even my normal routines around the house got sloppy, and I could tell I wasn’t just going to fix it by trying harder.
How often would you say these feelings of being down and empty are happening - is it most of the day or just some of the day?
Most of the day, I’d say. After that burst of energy wore off, it was like somebody pulled the plug on me. I’d just sit at the table staring at my coffee, feeling empty… and ashamed, honestly.
Have you had any periods in the last two weeks where you felt better for at least a couple of days?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a stretch where I felt better for a couple days straight. Maybe little moments here and there, but nothing that lasted.
Are there any activities that you still find pleasure in or look forward to?

Not really, no. The stuff that usually helps me settle down—fishing, going through my old vinyl records, tailgating, even checking on my home-brew—it all just feels like another chore now. I don’t really look forward to it like I used to.
Do you feel like you've been fidgety or restless, or have you been feeling like you're moving in slow motion most of the time?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself pacing or anything like that. Maybe I’ve been a bit slower getting around, but I couldn’t say it’s most of the time.
Would you say you've lost a significant amount of weight, like more than 5% of your body weight, over the past month?

I don’t know the exact number, but yeah, I think I’ve dropped some. Most days I have to remind myself to eat, and my jeans are definitely looser. Supper just kind of sits there and feels like too much trouble.
Do you feel like you're moving in slow motion most of the time?
I don’t think so. I mean, I feel a little slowed down here and there, but I wouldn’t say it’s most of the time.
Have you been feeling fidgety or restless?
Not really. I haven’t noticed myself being fidgety or unable to sit still. If anything, I’m just kind of… normal in that way, I guess.
Would you say these feelings of being down and empty have been present every day since they started?
Yeah… pretty much every day after that energy wore off. I just felt like someone pulled the plug on me. I’d sit there staring at my coffee, feeling empty and ashamed.
Would you say these feelings of being down and empty are interfering with your ability to work or take care of things at home most of the time?

Yeah, it has. I fell behind on bills and missed calls I was supposed to return, appointments too. And I needed to be looking for work, but I just couldn’t keep it going steadily. Even stuff at home, my usual routines, got sloppy. It got to where I knew I wasn’t just going to fix it by trying harder.
Would you say these feelings of being down and empty are present nearly all day, or are there parts of the day where you feel somewhat better?

It was most of the day, yeah. After that energy was gone, I just felt drained, like the plug had been pulled. I’d sit at the table staring at my coffee, feeling empty and kind of ashamed. Sometimes I might get distracted for a little bit, but it didn’t really lift much.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly or having difficulty getting started on things more often than not?
I’m not really sure. I mean, I’ve had trouble getting started on things, yeah, but I don’t know if I was actually moving slower. It’s more like I’d sit there and not get going.
Do you think you've been moving slower than usual most of the time since these feelings started?
I’m not sure I’d say I was moving slower most of the time. I just know I had a hard time getting myself started. Once I was up and doing something, I don’t really know if I looked slower or not.
Do you think your movements have been slower than normal most of the time since you started feeling this way?
I honestly haven’t noticed that my movements are slower most of the time. It’s more that I don’t feel like starting things, but I can’t really say I’m moving slower than normal.
